feeds.title: History Today
feeds.description: History Today is the world's leading serious history magazine. We publish the world's leading scholars, on all periods, regions, and themes of history.

feeds.title: Ancient Origins
feeds.description: The goal of Ancient Origins is to highlight recent archaeological discoveries, peer-reviewed academic research and evidence, as well as offering alternative viewpoints and explanations of science, archaeology, mythology, religion and history around the globe.

feeds.title: Ancient Pages
feeds.description: Founded in 2009, Ancient Pages is today one of the world's largest sites covering all about the ancient world. If you are interested in ancient mysteries, history, myths, legends, sacred writings, Biblical mysteries, and archaeology news - then you have come to the right place.

feeds.title: Following Hadrian
feeds.description: My name is Carole Raddato. I love to share with other history fans all the incredible facts and stories that I discover throughout my journeys. I am neither a professional photographer nor an ancient history scholar, but I hope that everybody can enjoy my photos.

feeds.title: The History Blog
feeds.description: Hello, I am Livius. I created this history blog page because my interests are primarily European ancient and medieval. Here I am providing general blogs on history, historical podcasts, historical illustrations, ancient books, and many more. I also intend to make a note of all the topically relevant books I read, and a list of all the topically relevant books sitting in a pile glaring at me.

feeds.title: A Collection of Unmitigated Pedantry Blog
feeds.description: Take a look at history and popular culture in A Collection of Unmitigated Pedantry blog by Dr. Bret C. Devereaux, an ancient historian specializing in the Roman economy and military.

feeds.title: On History Blog
feeds.description: On History is a digital magazine produced by the Institute of Historical Research, the national centre for the study of history in the UK. Our aim is to publish accessible and engaging articles that reflect on contemporary issues facing our discipline and deepen public understanding of the past.

feeds.title: Active History
feeds.description: Read amusing articles, historical anecdotes, and other stories in this space. Active History is a resource to help connect historians with the public, policymakers, and the media. We publish short papers by historians on a range of topics and blog posts on historians that engage with the internet and the public sphere.

feeds.title: The Unwritten Record Blog
feeds.description: The Unwritten Record is the National Archives and Records Administration's blog dedicated to special media holdings. The blog features information on fascinating finds, new accessions, preservation projects, and rediscoveries across the agency's non-textual holdings.

feeds.title: IU Libraries Blog » IUB Archives
feeds.description: The University Archives is a department within the IU Library system. As archives, our primary mission is to collect, organize, preserve and make accessible records documenting Indiana University's origins and development and the activities and achievements of its officers, faculty, students, alumni, and benefactors.

feeds.title: Folger Shakespeare Library Blog
feeds.description: The Collation is a gathering of useful information and observations from staff and researchers of the Folger Shakespeare Library. The Folger is a world-class center for scholarship, learning, culture, and the arts, and this blog seeks to present bite-sized glimpses of the materials found within our walls, along with the questions and answers they prompt.

feeds.title: Boundary Stones
feeds.description: A blog about local history in Washington, D.C., suburban Maryland and northern Virginia.These pages (or pixels!) seek to uncover and share some of the stories that have helped to shape our community over the years -- some serious stuff, some light stuff, some photos, and even some videos.

feeds.title: History Collections Blog
feeds.description: Find out more about history collections and History Day. The History Collections website and the annual History Day are a collaborative initiative of the Institute of Historical Research and Senate House Library alongside members of the History Research Libraries Committee.

feeds.title: Carnegie Museum of Natural History Blog
feeds.description: Carnegie Museum of Natural History, one of the four Carnegie Museums of Pittsburgh, is among the top natural history museums in the country. It maintains, preserves, and interprets an extraordinary collection of artifacts, objects, and scientific specimens used to broaden understanding of evolution, conservation, and biodiversity.

feeds.title: An Historian About Town
feeds.description: I'm Jessica. I'm the Historian, and I am here to celebrate all things history, style, culture! Welcome to An Historian About Town, where you can find history, culture, and style! I believe that history, culture, and style should always be accessible, no matter where you are. We all have a history, and we are all history in the making.

feeds.title: History Sidebar Blog
feeds.description: Writings on history and the production of history by David. David is a consulting historian doing oral histories, historical research, and historic preservation work.

feeds.title: Jaunting Jen
feeds.description: I'm Jen. Teacher, historian, traveler, yogi, bread-maker. Army Veteran with Multiple Sclerosis. This is a place to explore the history, travel, and everything else. History is cool, if you know where to look.

feeds.title: Frog in a Well
feeds.description: On this blog, a group of students and scholars will post entries related to the history of Japan or other topics relevant to its study.

feeds.title: Process: A Blog for American History
feeds.description: Process is the blog of the Organization of American Historians, The Journal of American History, and The American Historian, dedicated to exploring the process of doing history and the multifaceted ways of engaging with the U.S. past.

feeds.title: Voyager of History
feeds.description: This blog is a selection of interesting things I've come across during my history research. I have a wide interest in history ranging from Wars of the Roses, country houses, Stuarts, Georgians, Louis XIV, Napoleon and criminals. So expect to see a bit of everything on here, with a focus on little known stories.

feeds.title: Just History Posts
feeds.description: Just History Posts was started after the author, Gemma Hollman, graduated with her Masters in Medieval History. Just History Posts was a way to share the interesting things she had learnt throughout her studies. This blog explores topics in more depth, covering great people, world wonders, social and political history, and even a war against emus.

feeds.title: World History Blog
feeds.description: World History Blog - Providing you with stories of the past, interesting historical facts, and analysis of historical events!

feeds.title: J. History of Ideas Blog
feeds.description: The blog of the Journal of the History of Ideas, committed to diverse and wide-ranging intellectual history.The JHI defines intellectual history expansively and ecumenically, including the histories of philosophy, literature and the arts, the natural and social sciences, religion, and political thought.

feeds.title: Legal History Blog
feeds.description: scholarship, news and new ideas in legal history

feeds.title: Historical Britain Blog
feeds.description: In this blog Mercedes Rochelle talks everything about Historical Fiction.

feeds.title: Royal Historical Society Blog » Historical Transactions
feeds.description: The blog provides an online space for the Royal Historical Society to share news and discussion about its work, and for historians to discuss their research, methodological ideas, and reflections on history, in its widest sense.

feeds.title: The History Reader Blog
feeds.description: A History Blog by @StMartinsPress, offering articles, interviews, and further reading for history buffs and book lovers everywhere, from ancient times to today.

feeds.title: Living London History Blog
feeds.description: Sharing London's curiosities, hidden gems and historical walks, oddities and self-guided walks to help curious wanderers explore the city. The focus is on the history that is hiding in plain sight and helping Londoners and visitors better connect with the history of this incredible city.

feeds.title: History is Now Magazine Blog
feeds.description: We're a site that creates a variety of exclusive modern international and American history content! We create free history audio podcasts as part of History in 28-minutes, a magazine called History is Now, and books as part of Required History. Our works explain some of history's most important events concisely and quickly.

feeds.title: History Through Fiction Blog
feeds.description: History Through Fiction is an independent press publishing high quality fiction that is rooted in accurate and detailed historical research. History Through Fiction seeks to provide readers with compelling narratives that also act as valuable historical resources.

feeds.title: The History Quill Blog
feeds.description: The History Quill was founded with the aim of providing dedicated support to historical fiction writers at every stage of the writing process. There're here because of there deep-rooted passion for history and the stories it inspires.

feeds.title: Wearing History Blog
feeds.description: Wearing History is a Vintage Revival Clothing, Sewing Patterns Blog by Lauren. This blog is a journal of my journey with sewing and costume history, including research, projects, endeavors, and miscellaneous adventures.

feeds.title: Improbable Voices Blog
feeds.description: Improbable Voices

feeds.title: Teaching American History Blog
feeds.description: TeachingAmericanHistory.org is history and civics resource website designed for use by K-12 teachers, college faculty, students, and the public at large. It features a searchable library containing thousands of original documents spanning American history from the Colonial Era through the present, primary source document-based lesson plans designed for use in education.

feeds.title: Pieces of History Blog
feeds.description: Pieces of History brings you the latest discoveries from the vast holdings of the Archives of more than 15 billion pages of records, miles and miles of tape and film, and a growing number of electronic records. We also bring to you information about the agency itself from our creation in 1934 to the establishment of the most recent Presidential library. Join us as we share stories from the National Archives!

feeds.title: CuriosSpot
feeds.description: Drive through ancient history, places, and myths! Curiosspot is a blog dedicated to ancient history and enriching tales and brings you stories of human origins, natural wonders, Fascinating architecture, spooky stories, and all types of mysteries!

feeds.title: The Magic Trawler
feeds.description: Welcome aboard 'The Magic Trawler' where we like to cast a very wide net over the last 500 years of Modern History and identify how germanely it explains today's social & political culture.

feeds.title: Story Chronicles
feeds.description: Story Chronicles is your gateway to the enthralling world of world history and ancient history. Delve into the depths of time as we embark on a journey of Cultural Heritage and magnificent History of places.

feeds.title: BBC History Research Blog
feeds.description: Every year the BBC opens its archives to a wide range of academics researching the BBC's role in national and international history. Their research leads to bestselling books, academic papers and in-depth journalistic articles. This blog reveals the variety of BBC themes explored by academia.

feeds.title: Missouri State History Blog
feeds.description: Explore the blog for articles depicting the history of Missouri. Missouri State University is a public university system with students who come from all over Missouri, the nation, and the world. We are a close-knit community of passionate and steadfast learners committed to ethical leadership, cultural competence and community engagement.

feeds.title: National Library of Scotland Blog
feeds.description: A blog about the work and collections of the National Library of Scotland. From our curators, subject experts and guest bloggers. National Library of Scotland is a treasure trove of Scotland's knowledge, history, and culture with collections on every subject.

feeds.title: Facing Today
feeds.description: Welcome to Facing Today, a Facing History blog. Facing History and Ourselves combats racism and antisemitism by using history to teach tolerance in classrooms around the globe.

feeds.title: Appalachian History
feeds.description: Appalachian History has been digging up stories, quotes and anecdotes about the region since 2006. Special emphasis on the 1880s to 1950s time period, when the concept of 'Appalachia' as place emerged.

feeds.title: Thijs Porck Blog
feeds.description: Hello! I am a cultural historian of early medieval England, with a background in medieval history as well as English language and literature. On this website, you will find an overview of books and publications, conferences, teaching endeavours as well as my appearances in the media and my efforts to popularize my field (outreach).

feeds.title: Ancient Foods
feeds.description: Exploring the origins and history of food & drink around the world. My name is Joanna Linsley-Poe. I am a chef, artisan bread baker, ancient food historian, food archaeologist, and anthropologist as well as a writer. Although that sounds like quite a mouthful, I guess it's all about a love of history and food.

feeds.title: Sarah E. Bond
feeds.description: Musings on daily life in the ancient and early medieval Mediterranean by Sarah E. Bond.

feeds.title: Susan Higginbotham
feeds.description: I'm Susan. I write historical fiction and nonfiction set in medieval and Tudor England and, most recently, nineteenth-century America. As a writer of biographical fiction, one of my main goals is to avoid the stereotypes, myths, and misconceptions that have gathered around historical figures over the centuries.

feeds.title: Natural History Museum Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to the blog from the Natural History Museum in London, where our curators, researchers, librarians, staff, and volunteers will be bringing you a behind-the-scenes look at what they do and why. The Museum is a world-class visitor attraction and a leading science research center. We use our unique collections and unrivaled expertise to tackle the biggest challenges facing the world today. We care for more than 80 million objects spanning billions of years and welcome more than five million visitors annually.

feeds.title: You're History!
feeds.description: I'll be using this place to organize and share all the things I love doing. Among the topics, I like to study and write about are folklore, medieval life and times, American history up to the end of the Civil War, Connecticut and New England, travel, animals, plants, and gardening. I also will be posting reviews of books I've enjoyed.

feeds.title: Women of History
feeds.description: This is a site providing biographies of some of the fascinating women who have graced the pages of history, in addition to articles pertaining to history, and medieval and modern women. By Melisende - a passionate bibliophile, avid reader, writer, independent researcher, history buff, coffee drinker, cat owner.

feeds.title: Rediscovering Black History Blog
feeds.description: The blog of the Black history guide, sharing records relating to the Black Experience at the National Archives.

feeds.title: The Local History Blogger
feeds.description: with Laura

feeds.title: The Archivist History Blog
feeds.description: ? Follow My Blog Get new content delivered directly to your inbox.

feeds.title: University Collections Blog
feeds.description: The University Library's Special Collections blog highlights items from the collections to explore their past and context. The University of St Andrews is a public university in St Andrews, Fife, Scotland. It is the oldest of the four ancient universities of Scotland.

feeds.title: The History of Parliament
feeds.description: Blogging on parliament, politics, and people, from the History of Parliament. The History of Parliament is a major academic project to create a scholarly reference work describing the members, constituencies, and activities of the Parliament of England and the United Kingdom.

feeds.title: AncientBlogger
feeds.description: Hi there, I'm an ancient blogger and this is my site with different ancient history content for all levels of interest. Vlogs, podcasts, and articles. It's all here!

feeds.title: Art History News
feeds.description: A history of art blog covering news stories on art history matters. The blog covers news of auctions from the likes of Sotheby's, Christie's and Bonhams of old masters such as Van Dyck, Rubens, Titian, Raphael, Michelangelo and Leonardo, British artists such as Thomas Gainsborough, Thomas Lawrence, Joshua Reynolds, George Romney and William Hogarth, as well as modern and contemporary artists.

feeds.title: Texas Historical Commission Blog
feeds.description: The Texas Historical Commission (THC) is the state agency for historic preservation. We save the real places that tell the real stories of Texas.
